notations.effect: The same edge as the plain form. The alias changes the text, never the target.
The same edge as the plain form: the anchor is kept for display and dropped in resolution. Two links to two sections of one note are two links to the same note.

notations.effect: Becomes the same edge as a wikilink. The target is reduced to its basename without extension and resolved by slug, so a path with folders in it resolves to the note and not to the path.

notations.effect: NEVER becomes an edge. Anything with a scheme or a host is external, and the graph is about the notes of this vault. Use it freely for sources; do not use it expecting a connection.

notations.syntax: `[[Target note]]` inside a code span or fence
notations.example: Write a link as `[[Lei 14.133]]` in the body.
notations.effect: A link inside code is an example, not a reference, and produces no edge.
Becomes an attribute you can filter and count by, and a search filter written as `maturity:evergreen`. The vocabulary is yours: no key is special.

notations.syntax: key: [one, two]  ·  or a dash list under the key
notations.effect: Becomes an attribute with several values, each one filterable on its own.
Becomes a boolean attribute, which is what makes "what has nobody reviewed" answerable.
Becomes a date attribute, queryable by prefix: the year, the month or the day. An ISO 8601 date is recognised as a date; other formats are not.

Reserved: alternative spellings of this note, which join the search index and rank as the title does. They do NOT resolve wikilinks, and that is a decision rather than a gap: resolution is behaviour, and an alias collision can be created by editing a third note that is neither end of the link, moving an existing edge with nothing on screen saying so. A link that does not resolve is at least visible, as a pending link.
Reserved: the subjects of this note. This is where a tag lives in this profile, and it is filterable and countable like any other list attribute.
Reserved: what the author states about when the content came to be. It is never the history of the file; an implementation that knows the real history treats that as authoritative.
Reserved: what the author states about when the content was last revised. Like `created`, it is a statement about the content and not the history of the file.

notations.syntax: title: Whatever the note is called
notations.effect: NOT reserved and NOT special. The title of a note is structural: `title:` never renames it and never takes part in link resolution. As an ordinary attribute it is prose that is unique per note, which the cardinality ceiling stops indexing on its own.

notations.syntax: key: a whole sentence, longer than forty characters
notations.example:
---
summary: This note explains the general rule of direct contracting and its exceptions.
---

Body.
notations.effect: Is read and DISCARDED. Above forty characters a value is prose, not a category, and an attribute of unique sentences would be a list of everything. Put prose in the body.

Carries NO meaning in this profile: neither an edge nor an attribute, and rendered as plain text. To group notes by subject write `tags:` in the frontmatter; to connect a note to a subject worth a note of its own, write [[subject]].

notations.effect: A blockquote whose first line begins with `[!type]` is drawn as a callout, not as a quotation with a marker in front of it. The five GitHub alert types are recognised and the vocabulary is open. A `[!type]` inside a code fence is not a callout.
A fenced block whose info string is `mermaid` is rendered as a diagram. A reader that cannot render it shows the source, never nothing.

The reading surface shows the content of the target in place, one level deep: an embed inside embedded content is drawn as a link. The bytes never change, and tools return the `![[...]]` that was written.

notations.syntax: [[A note that does not exist yet]]
notations.example: See [[A note nobody has written]] for the rest.
notations.effect: A wikilink whose target does not exist is shown as visibly pending, never as a broken link and never hidden. It is the gesture of writing the note that is missing.
GFM task list items. A reading surface may let a person toggle one, and a toggle writes back exactly the one character that changed, never a reformatted note.

notations.example: The exception is ==only for the cases listed in article 75==.
notations.effect: Marks a run of text. Rendered as marked, with the `==` never shown as characters. It carries no meaning beyond emphasis: no edge, no attribute, no index entry.

notations.example: The rule holds. %%check this against the 2027 revision%%
notations.effect: Text the author does not want read on the page: it disappears from the reading surface and stays in the bytes. A tool that returns the note returns it, and an export writes it, so an agent sees what a person on the page does not. That asymmetry is deliberate and is declared here rather than discovered.

notations.example: The rule is stated once, here. ^article-75
notations.effect: Names the block it ends, so an embed can resolve to that block instead of to the whole note. The identifier is never rendered as text. It names nothing outside its own note.

Embeds the named block rather than the whole note. The edge it produces is exactly the edge `[[Target note]]` produces: the graph does not tell an embed from a reference apart, and does not tell a block embed from either.

notations.example: The ceiling is $n \log n$ in the worst case.
notations.effect: Rendered as mathematics. A `$` that is not opening or closing a formula stays text: a price and a shell variable are not formulas.
Rendered as mathematics, as a block of its own.

notations.example: The formula is H~2~O, and the area is 3 m^2^.
notations.effect: NOT part of this profile, and deliberately so. GitHub writes these with raw HTML, which this profile does not render; the Pandoc forms render in no vault editor, so a note written with them would look broken in every other tool its author uses, and the `^` form would collide with a block identifier. Write the character itself when it exists, or a formula.

NOT rendered. Stored and returned exactly as written, and shown as text. This is a security boundary and not a rendering preference: a vault is written by several people and by agents, and a page that renders arbitrary HTML out of it is a script injection whose trigger is written by whoever wrote the note.
